question: Should OpenClaw claim `auth` as a plugin-yielding built-in root solely to provide the `openclaw auth list` convenience alias?
rationale: The existing canonical command already solves profile inspection, while a new top-level root creates a permanent CLI and plugin-ownership contract that code correctness alone cannot authorize.

options.title: Keep the canonical command
options.body: Decline the new root and continue documenting `openclaw models auth list`, avoiding a new collision-sensitive CLI contract.

options.title: Accept the yielding alias
options.body: Approve `auth` as a plugin-first fallback root, then require exact-head green checks and live proof of both ownership paths before merge.

recommendation.title: Keep the canonical command
recommendation.body: Decline the new root and continue documenting `openclaw models auth list`, avoiding a new collision-sensitive CLI contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The available merged history ties this decision most directly to the plugin-root registration and overlap contract they introduced.
